guide.title: A week in Boston
guide.author: Nate Bird
guide.summary: Seven days of the Freedom Trail and the North End, oysters and cannoli, great museums, Fenway and walks along the Charles.

places.name: Omni Parker House
places.notes: America's oldest continuously operating hotel, on the Freedom Trail. Boston cream pie was invented here.

places.name: The Liberty, a Luxury Collection Hotel
places.notes: A former jail, now a striking hotel at the foot of Beacon Hill. Have a drink in Alibi, in the old drunk tank.

places.name: Fairmont Copley Plaza
places.notes: A 1912 grand hotel on Copley Square, with a resident Labrador who greets guests.

places.name: The Verb Hotel
places.notes: A rock-and-roll motel by Fenway Park, with a heated pool and vinyl in every room.

places.name: Neptune Oyster
places.notes: A tiny oyster bar with the city's best hot lobster roll. Go at opening to skip the wait.

places.name: Union Oyster House
places.notes: America's oldest restaurant, serving since 1826. Sit at the raw bar downstairs.

places.name: Giacomo's
places.notes: Red-sauce Italian in a small, loud room. Cash only, and a line, but it moves.

places.name: Regina Pizzeria
places.notes: The original North End pizza oven, firing since 1926.

places.name: Mike's Pastry
places.notes: The famous cannoli in the white box tied with string.

places.name: Modern Pastry
places.notes: The locals' cannoli, filled to order, across the street from Mike's. Try both.

places.name: Quincy Market
places.notes: A long food hall behind Faneuil Hall. Clam chowder in a bread bowl, eaten on the steps.

places.name: Row 34
places.notes: A working-class oyster bar in the Seaport, with a great beer list.

places.name: Toro
places.notes: Busy, delicious Spanish tapas. Order the grilled corn with aioli and cheese.

places.name: Myers + Chang
places.notes: A playful Asian diner from the team behind Flour. The dumplings and the tea-smoked ribs.

places.name: Flour Bakery + Cafe
places.notes: Joanne Chang's bakery. The sticky buns are the thing to order.

places.name: Tatte Bakery & Cafe
places.notes: A bright bakery on Charles Street. Breakfast before a Beacon Hill walk.

places.name: Santarpio's Pizza
places.notes: No-frills pizza and grilled lamb skewers in East Boston since 1903.

places.name: Sullivan's Castle Island
places.address: 2080 William J Day Blvd, Boston, MA 02127
places.notes: Hot dogs and fried clams by the water since 1951. Open from late February to November.

places.name: Bell in Hand Tavern
places.notes: Founded in 1795 by the town crier, and still pouring on the Freedom Trail.

places.name: Bleacher Bar
places.notes: A bar under Fenway's bleachers, with a window right onto center field.

places.name: Paul Revere House
places.notes: Downtown Boston's oldest house, built around 1680, where Revere lived when he made his ride.

places.name: Old North Church
places.notes: Where the two lanterns hung in 1775. The behind-the-scenes tour goes into the crypt.

places.name: Faneuil Hall
places.notes: A 1742 meeting hall where colonists argued for independence. Rangers give free talks upstairs.

places.name: Massachusetts State House
places.notes: The gold-domed State House. Free tours on weekdays.

places.name: USS Constitution Museum
places.notes: Board Old Ironsides, the oldest commissioned warship afloat, then see the museum next door.

places.name: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston
places.notes: One of the great American museums. Don't miss the Sargent murals over the rotunda.

places.name: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
places.notes: A Venetian palace built around a flowering courtyard, with the empty frames of the 1990 heist.

places.name: Boston Public Library
places.notes: The 1895 McKim Building and its green-lamped Bates Hall. Free art and architecture tours.

places.name: Trinity Church
places.notes: H.H. Richardson's 1877 church on Copley Square, glowing inside with murals and stained glass.

places.name: Fenway Park
places.notes: The oldest ballpark in the majors, opened in 1912. Take the tour if there's no game.

places.name: New England Aquarium
places.notes: A four-story ocean tank with sea turtles, and whale-watching boats leaving from the wharf.

places.name: John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum
places.notes: JFK's life and presidency in an I.M. Pei building on the harbor.

places.name: Institute of Contemporary Art
places.notes: Contemporary art in a building cantilevered over the harbor. The view from the Mediatheque is a highlight.

places.name: Harvard Yard
places.notes: Walk the yard, rub John Harvard's shoe, then browse the bookshops of Harvard Square.

places.name: MIT Museum
places.notes: Robots, holograms and kinetic sculpture, in a new building in Kendall Square.

places.name: Boston Common
places.notes: America's oldest public park, and the start of the Freedom Trail. Follow the red brick line.

places.name: Boston Public Garden
places.notes: Swan boats on the lagoon in summer, and the Make Way for Ducklings statues all year.

places.name: Charles River Esplanade
places.notes: A long riverside path with sailboats and the Hatch Shell. Lovely at sunset.

places.name: Rose Kennedy Greenway
places.notes: A park built over the old elevated highway, with fountains, a carousel and food trucks.

places.name: Arnold Arboretum
places.notes: Harvard's free arboretum. Climb Peters Hill for a view of the skyline, and come in May for the lilacs.

places.name: Castle Island
places.address: 2010 William J Day Blvd, Boston, MA 02127
places.notes: A loop around Fort Independence, with planes landing overhead. Pair it with Sullivan's.
